Build one crew.cluster SLURM controller per model

Source: R/pipeline-orchestration.R
build_slurm_controllers.Rd

One controller/worker group per model (ADR 0001) — each worker starts ollama serve once via ollama_worker_script_lines() and reuses it across that model's research-question x context-variant x granularity x include_headlines cells. Splice the result into crew::crew_controller_group() and pass to tar_option_set(controller = ...).

Usage

build_slurm_controllers(
  models,
  resources = read_slurm_resources(),
  host = dispatcher_host(),
  seconds_launch = 3600
)

Arguments

models

A character vector of Ollama model identifiers, or a tibble as returned by read_models() (the model column is extracted)

resources

A list as returned by read_slurm_resources(); per-model overrides are resolved via resolve_slurm_resources() keyed off model names. A resolved gres_gpu field (e.g. "gpu:2") is passed to ollama_worker_script_lines() rather than spliced into crew.cluster::crew_options_slurm(), which has no matching argument; it defaults to "gpu:1" when absent

host

Address the dispatcher listens on and workers dial; see dispatcher_host() for why crew's own default isn't used

seconds_launch

Seconds crew waits for a launched worker to connect before treating it as lost and relaunching. Must cover GPU queue wait, but stay well below the dispatcher job's walltime: crew's default (86400) makes a worker that dies before connecting leave the dispatcher hanging silently until walltime (ADR 0006). If a worker dies before connecting (e.g. module load fails, Ollama server fails to start), crew will relaunch it endlessly until either the worker connects or the dispatcher walltime is reached; this is a known behavior in crew 1.3.3, accepted per ADR 0007

Value

A list of crew_controller_slurm objects, one per model, each named for its model

Details

Each worker's SLURM stdout/stderr is captured to crew-logs/<sanitised model>_<job id>.log (relative to the working directory targets::tar_make() is run from) — crew.cluster defaults this to /dev/null otherwise, which silently discards module-load, Ollama startup, and worker errors. The crew-logs/ directory is created here (not left to SLURM) because a missing --output directory makes sbatch fail the job immediately.
